name: What is the difference between a shell space and a second-generation space for an office build-out?

mainEntity.name: What is the difference between a shell space and a second-generation space for an office build-out?

acceptedAnswer.text: A 'shell space' is a raw, unfinished commercial unit, often with just exterior walls, a roof, and a concrete slab. It requires a complete build-out including all interior walls, flooring, ceilings, and utility installations. A 'second-generation space' is a previously occupied and built-out office. It may already have existing walls, finishes, and infrastructure, which can reduce the scope and cost of a new build-out if the existing layout aligns with new needs, but often still requires significant renovation.
acceptedAnswer.description: A shell space is raw and unfinished, requiring a complete build-out. A second-generation space is previously built-out, potentially reducing renovation scope and cost.
